clue.text: Covering article in duplicate

indicators.note: in tells us the article is placed inside the word for a duplicate

parts.note: a duplicate is a copy
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the cover on a document that was made twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: A canopy is an overhead cloth or roof serving as a covering.

clue.text: Arrive with side-splitting plays!

parts.note: to come is to arrive
one who dies laughing is in side-splitting fits

explanation.surface: Turn up for a hilarious evening at the theatre!
explanation.walkthrough: 'side-splitting' looks like it describes the plays, but it gives DIES, as in dying with laughter; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedies are humorous stage works, a kind of drama.

clue.text: Speed needed after all points bulletin

indicators.note: after says the speed word comes behind the compass letters

parts.note: N, E, W and S are all four points of the compass
flash means great speed, as in 'in a flash'

explanation.surface: A broadcast warns drivers to slow down everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed' is a link; 'all points' means every compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: A newsflash is a brief urgent news report, a broadcast bulletin.

clue.text: One pretends to sit on centre court chair at last

parts.note: to sit for a portrait is to pose

indicators.note: centre means the middle letter of court
at last means the final letter of chair

explanation.surface: A show-off takes a seat at the umpire's chair on centre court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' picks U from court and 'at last' picks R from chair; 'to' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseur affects attitudes or talents they lack, a pretender.

clue.text: Suffered from mistakes in dosage

indicators.note: mistakes made with the letters mean they are jumbled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A patient was in pain because the nurse got the dose wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakes' signals an anagram of IN and DOSAGE together; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have agonised is to have endured torment, a synonym for suffered.

clue.text: All out attack under officer?

indicators.note: under in a down clue puts the attack word below the officer word

parts.note: a general is a senior army officer
a strike is an attack

explanation.surface: A military assault ordered by a commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' places STRIKE beneath GENERAL. 'All out' looks like a military push but is the cry of a union calling every worker out.
explanation.definitionFit: When every worker downs tools across industries, the stoppage is total.

clue.text: Becoming insensitive and counting without hesitation

indicators.note: without means the hesitation is taken out of the counting word

parts.note: numbering is counting
er is a hesitation sound

explanation.surface: Someone loses feeling while counting smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes ER from NUMBERING; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbing means losing sensation, going dead to feeling.

clue.text: Wrong area on island mountain

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: Something bad happened on a remote peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinai is the Biblical peak where Moses received the commandments.

clue.text: The purpose of French-to communicate non-verbally?

parts.note: de is French for of
to sign is to communicate with gestures

explanation.surface: Why would a French speaker use sign language?
explanation.walkthrough: 'The purpose of' seems one phrase, but 'of French' gives DE; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Design can mean intention, as in 'by design', meaning on purpose.

clue.text: Moans about sort of house accommodating student

indicators.note: accommodating means holding something inside, so the student goes within the house word

parts.note: a mews house is a converted stable dwelling in a British back lane
L is the learner plate letter, used for a student

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a type of dwelling with a lodger in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accommodating' puts L inside MEWS; 'about' is a link. A mews is a London-style row of former stables turned into homes.
explanation.definitionFit: To mewl is to whimper or cry feebly, much like moaning.

clue.text: Items found in Roman ruins sent abroad

indicators.note: ruins says the word Roman is wrecked and rearranged
abroad means scattered widely, so the word sent is mixed in too

explanation.surface: Archaeologists unearth objects among old Italian remains and ship them overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruins' and 'abroad' together signal an anagram of ROMAN and SENT; 'found in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornaments are decorative objects, a kind of item.

clue.text: Perhaps no endings that produced "Brief Encounter"

indicators.note: produced means made into something new, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A classic film perhaps had no satisfying conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'produced' signals an anagram of NO ENDINGS THAT; 'Perhaps' warns the definition is an example. 'Brief Encounter' is a famous 1945 British romantic film.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-lived sexual liaison lasting a single evening is literally a brief encounter.

clue.text: Spread out if feuds develop

indicators.note: develop means change form, so the letters of if and feuds rearrange

explanation.surface: Quarrels escalate and widen into something bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develop' signals an anagram of IF and FEUDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Diffuse as a verb means to scatter or disperse widely.

clue.text: Call about trouble with fence

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the call word goes round the trouble word

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: A neighbour phones to complain about a dispute over a boundary fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call' looks like the definition, but the fence is the definition and 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A railing is a barrier of bars, a type of fence.

clue.text: Feel a need to conceal panache

indicators.note: to conceal means the letters sit buried inside the words feel a need

explanation.surface: Someone wants to hide their flamboyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to conceal' shows the answer sitting inside 'fe(EL A N)eed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is stylish flair and verve, much like panache.

clue.text: Medicine ball (old) taken by force

parts.note: a pill is a dose of medicine and also slang for a ball
aged means old

explanation.surface: A piece of gym kit, worn with age, was seized.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medicine ball' looks like gym equipment, but PILL is both a tablet of medicine and a slang word for a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: To pillage is to plunder, seizing goods by violence.

clue.text: Making a mistake in the German gun

indicators.note: in says the mistake word is put inside the German word

parts.note: der is the German for the
erring is making a mistake

explanation.surface: A German soldier blunders with his weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small short-barrelled pocket pistol.

clue.text: Just the cake for a money mad person?

parts.note: dough is slang for money
a nut is slang for a crazy person

explanation.surface: A treat suits someone obsessed with cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A doughnut is a ring of fried sweet batter, a small cake.

clue.text: Popular photographs from experts

parts.note: hot means currently popular or in demand
shots are photographs

explanation.surface: Fashionable pictures taken by skilled professionals.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotshots are highly skilled, successful people, a slangy term for experts.

clue.text: Crying time, and getting a severe scolding!

parts.note: an earful is a severe telling-off

explanation.surface: After a long dressing-down, someone breaks into sobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and getting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearful means weeping or close to weeping.

clue.text: The group to admit religious instruction?

indicators.note: admit means let in, so the word to takes the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: RI is the British school abbreviation for religious instruction

explanation.surface: Should the band allow some Bible teaching?
explanation.walkthrough: In British schools, religious education lessons were once called religious instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a set of three, such as a musical group of three players.

clue.text: Old tower across the river has fish

indicators.note: across means spanning, so the tower word straddles the river letter

parts.note: Babel is the ancient Biblical tower
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An ancient tower beside a river has fish swimming by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' puts BABEL around R; 'the' and 'has' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: The barbel is a freshwater carp-family species with whiskers.

clue.text: Write carelessly, seeing son grovel

parts.note: to crawl is to grovel

explanation.surface: A parent scribbles a note after seeing their boy fawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrawl is to scribble untidily.

clue.text: Struggles to pronounce an idiomatic expression

indicators.note: to pronounce means to say out loud, so we want what the words sound like

parts.note: an idiomatic expression is a phrase, so a phrase

explanation.surface: Someone has trouble saying a figure of speech correctly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to pronounce' signals that 'a phrase' spoken out loud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Affrays are public fights or brawls, a sense of struggles.

clue.text: Pretend to be foreign-or not, perhaps

indicators.note: not means the little word or is left out of foreign

explanation.surface: Faking an accent to seem from abroad, or maybe not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes OR from FOREIGN; 'to be' and 'perhaps' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To feign is to fake or simulate.

clue.text: Slowly advancing and stealing off the leader

indicators.note: off the leader means the first letter is dropped from the word for stealing

parts.note: pinching is slang for stealing

explanation.surface: A thief creeps forward after robbing the front-runner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off the leader' removes the first letter P from PINCHING.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving a short distance at a time is creeping forward by small amounts.

clue.text: Short suit, for example, could be held in one

definitions.text: for example, could be held in one

parts.note: brief means short
a suit is a lawsuit, a legal case

explanation.surface: A tailor says a cropped outfit might be kept in a bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' seems to be clothing but is a lawsuit; the definition says a short suit (a lawyer's brief) could be carried in a leather document bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer's papers on a matter are carried in a flat document bag of this kind.

clue.text: Article about river travel is a gas

indicators.note: about means going round, so the article encloses the other pieces

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
R is the map abbreviation for river
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about a river trip is great fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link. 'A gas' looks like slang for great fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a noble element, an inert gas in the air.

clue.text: Country girl grown up became a pub manageress

parts.note: a land is a country
a girl who has grown up is a lady

explanation.surface: A rural lass matured and ended up running a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'became' is a link. In Britain the woman who runs a pub is traditionally called its landlady.
explanation.definitionFit: The landlady of a British pub is the woman who keeps and runs it.

clue.text: Girl with time for French wine

parts.note: Clare is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A woman trades her free time for a glass of wine from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Claret is the British name for red Bordeaux, a wine from France.
